arg.name: Advanced Research Grant (ARG)
tips: Two stages: a pre-proposal, then a full proposal for shortlisted applicants. The pre-proposal must state the big idea and its outcome plainly.

Headline criteria: originality, feasibility, clarity of outcomes, interdisciplinary integration and potential impact. The proposal is the primary basis of evaluation; past performance of the team is a secondary input.
Every Co-PI needs a defined contribution. A Co-PI in name only can be grounds for rejection at the pre-proposal stage.
Above ₹1 crore expect an additional level of technical review. Justify each major equipment line.
Up to ₹5 crore over up to 5 years. In general a PI may run only one ANRF project at a time.

ecrg.name: PM Early Career Research Grant (PM-ECRG)
tips: Up to ₹60 lakh plus overheads for three years. PM-ECRG replaces the earlier SERB Start-up Research Grant.
Applicants must not already hold an ECR, SRG, CRG/EMR or other SERB/ANRF grant. Co-PIs are not allowed (except for PIO/OCI applicants).
Show independence: the problem must be yours, distinct from your PhD or postdoc supervisor's programme.
Give a year-wise plan with realistic manpower (JRF/SRF) and lean on start-up facilities at your institute.

matrics.name: ARG-MATRICS
tips: For active researchers in mathematics, theoretical sciences and quantitative social sciences. The PI's credentials carry much of the weight.
Only one MATRICS proposal per applicant in a call.

other.name: Other ANRF programme (CoE, PAIR, MAHA, CRMRP…)
tips: Caps and eligibility differ widely between ANRF programmes: read the call document for this programme.
ANRF asks that work align with Viksit Bharat 2047. Name the national mission or sector the work serves and how industry or government partners take it forward.
